root.claim: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, disproving the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in that model.
root.method: Reduce the product to a cyclic convolution of radix digits evaluated by Fourier-type transforms, make the two costly ingredients of those transforms (address rearrangement and butterfly arithmetic) cost a power of the logarithm less than a full scan per level by two rank-saving tape procedures, then assemble the algorithm, prove exactness and total the cost.

motivation.text: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so both the movement and the arithmetic must be sped up.
